title: Skilldeck skill catalog, schema_version 1
description: The output of `skilldeck catalog --json`. Consumers must ignore properties they do not recognise: additive changes do not bump schema_version (see docs/catalog.md).

schema_version.description: Bumped only for a breaking change to this schema.

distribution.description: The skilldeck package the catalog describes, as `skilldeck provenance --json` reports it.

source_ref.description: The release tag the package was built from; null for a development build.

source_commit.description: The full commit the package was built from; null for a development build.

oneOf.description: A release build names both its tag and its commit.

skills.description: Every bundled skill exactly once, sorted by name (guarantees JSON Schema cannot express; see docs/catalog.md).

supported_agents.description: Agent names, sorted. New agents may appear without a schema_version bump.

canonical_sha256.description: The skill's canonical content digest, as recorded in the packaged content manifest and checked by `skilldeck provenance --verify`.

rendered_sha256.description: For each supported agent, the digest of the file skilldeck installs for it: after the sha256: prefix, exactly the hash= an install stamp records.

path.description: The skill directory in the source repository, as a POSIX path.

deprecated.description: null unless the skill is deprecated.

since.description: The skill version that first carried the deprecation.

replacement.description: The skill to use instead, or null.

capabilities.description: What the skill declares it may ask an agent to do (docs/authoring-skills.md#capabilities). A declaration for review that nothing enforces; anything not listed is not requested.

schema.description: The capability schema of the declaration. Changing it is a catalog change like any other (see docs/catalog.md).

read.description: none, diff (the changed files) or repo (any file in the repository).

write.description: none, or repo: the skill may edit files in the repository.

commands.description: Commands the skill may ask the agent to run, e.g. "git diff" (with any arguments); "<...>" stands for a command the project defines.

network.description: What the skill may contact, and why.

credentials.description: Secrets the skill asks the agent to read, pass on or send.

tools.description: Agent tools the skill needs beyond reading files and running its commands.

artifacts.description: Files the skill may create, as POSIX paths relative to the project root.
